messages:
maya: FYI PR #8123 changed the GH Actions workflow for terraform apply -> added a 'wait-for-argocd' step. After merging to staging we noticed long apply queues and ArgoCD apps stuck in 'syncing' for hours. Anyone seen this pattern before?

oliver: I think I saw the logs. infra-bot queued 6 applies for the infra workspace, but GH Actions concurrency didn't prevent parallel atlantis applies. At least two applies hit the same state lock and one timed out.

maya: Right — I suspected the GH Actions concurrency wasn't scoped to the atlantis workspace. The change was to add: 
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: infra-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
which is fine for deployments but doesn't map cleanly to atlantis workspaces.

sasha: Also the new step does `curl https://argocd.example.com/api/v1/applications/$APP/sync` and then polls until status=Synced. If the apply is queued, argocd never sees the new manifests — deadlock.

ben: Yep that's the race: GH Actions -> atlantis apply -> push manifests -> ArgoCD sync. If you wait for ArgoCD in the workflow before the apply completes (or while another apply holds the state lock), nothing progresses.

infra-bot: queued apply for workspace "staging-infra" (PR:8123)

oliver: Quick suggestion: make the GH Action concurrency group include the atlantis workspace name and PR number, e.g. `infra-${{ github.head_ref }}-staging`, so only one apply for that workspace can run. Also add a short backoff/retry when acquire-lock fails.

maya: Good call. Also maybe move the ArgoCD wait into a post-apply step that is triggered by atlantis webhooks (post-apply webhook -> workflows dispatch), instead of waiting synchronously inside the same GH job. That decouples the apply lock.

sasha: Implementation idea: let atlantis apply return immediately after success and post a status to the repo. Then a separate workflow with `on: status` or `repository_dispatch` does the ArgoCD sync+wait. That keeps applies small.

ben: Alternatively, use atlantis postapply hook in our atlantis.yaml to call an internal service that enqueues an argocd sync job. Simpler than wiring GH Actions events.

maya: I'm leaning to the separate workflow approach so we keep GH Action changes smaller. I'll open a small patch to change concurrency group and split the argocd wait.

oliver: One more: double-check our DynamoDB/S3 state lock TTLs. We had a few aborted runs holding locks for 30m because the runner lost connection. Lower TTL or add a watchdog to clear stale locks after 5m of failed heartbeats.

infra-bot: atlantis apply success for PR:8119 workspace: staging-infra (released by oliver) :party_parrot:

maya: Created PR #8132 with two commits: 1) change GH Actions concurrency to include workspace+branch, 2) split argocd wait into `post-apply-sync` workflow triggered by repo status. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8132

sasha: Thanks — I'll update the README and add a note in ops runbook about post-apply hooks and lock timeouts.

ben: Quick test plan: 1) patch concurrency only on a feature branch 2) open two parallel PRs that both target staging infra 3) ensure only one atlantis apply runs and second waits in queue 4) verify post-apply workflow runs independent of apply and completes argocd sync.

maya: Sounds good. If anyone wants to pair on the test tomorrow ping me. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

oliver: cheers. I'll also drop a short gist with a sample `concurrency` and a small retry wrapper for `atlantis apply`.

ben: tagging @sre as FYI about lock TTLs and potential watch-dog change.

maya: @sre noted, I'll add an incident-prep checklist in the runbook in case a lock TTL change causes any surprise reaps.

infra-bot: reminder: scheduled maintenance for DynamoDB table "tf-state-locks" tomorrow 03:00-04:00 UTC (may affect lock acquisition).

sasha: ok good to know, we'll avoid high-risk rollouts during that window.

maya: closing the loop — PR merged to staging with the concurrency change, observing behavior. Will report back if we see remaining hangs. Thanks all!
